result.verdict: Approve with changes. The guide now teaches the framework without depending on the records lesson, and most of its lifecycle, state and cleanup claims match application.md, state.md and events.md. Before the frozen pilot, fix two things: the task-shaped refresh guidance, which may leak benchmark answers, and missing instrumentation showing whether agents read the guide. Also tighten three accuracy points (restart and children, conditional disposal, error recovery order). The navigation fix counts as part of the treatment only if both conditions' snapshots are checked and reads are logged.
blockingIssues: Possible benchmark leakage. The 'Refresh data while someone is editing … Preserve the editor and its draft' row and the overlapping-refresh paragraph ('a retained owner may finish work while a panel is closed … a destroyed initiating View should not control its replacement') read like the answers to specific pilot tasks, not general framework concepts. Before freezing, have someone who has not seen the benchmark rubric check them. Otherwise, reword them as decisions to make, not prescribed outcomes. If they match rubric items, the pilot measures copying rather than understanding.

Exposure is not measured. The old pilot never recorded whether guided runs read the added guidance, so its 'all 6 lacked Application preparation' result tells us nothing about the guide. The new run proposal must (a) confirm, per condition, that the frozen snapshots contain the intended readme, quick-start and llms.txt links (the earlier bug removed them from both conditions), and (b) log which docs each run opened, so the analysis can tell 'guide read' apart from 'guide available'. Without this, restoring navigation cannot be evaluated as part of the treatment.
risks: Restart row leaves out children. Per application.md, restart's stop phase stops registered children, and 'Starting the parent again does not automatically reactivate that child.' Agents building retry at the parent level will lose child UI. Add: 'Registered children are stopped and must be started again explicitly.'

Disposal is conditional. The guide says owned state 'is disposed on destruction through the configured provider', and the destroy row says it 'disposes owned state'. state.md says disposeOwned is called only 'when provided'. The default provider may not dispose anything. Reword as 'disposed by the configured provider when it supports disposal.'

Error recovery order is missing. The guide says the caller decides recovery 'including cleanup of any partial UI' but not how. application.md requires awaiting stop() successfully before showing an error View in the intended Region. That ordering is the part agents get wrong, so state it.

Children started inside parent prepareStart: if parent preparation fails or is superseded, the parent's signal does not stop a child that was already started. application.md says children started during preparation may still need cleanup. The guide recommends this pattern without that caveat.

These claims are not covered by the supplied contracts and need checking against view.md, behavior.md and mnobject.md: that rendering a containing View destroys its child Views; that an el with template:false delegates events without a render; that a Behavior's lifetime follows its host; that MnObject destruction is synchronous.

Unverified link targets: api/view-runtime.md#child-events, setup.md#configure-once, and the existence of api/mnobject.md, api/behavior.md, api/collection-view.md and api/data-providers.md. A broken anchor inside a frozen pilot bundle quietly weakens the treatment.

Changing the guide content and its reading order (it moves ahead of records.md) in the same step means new results cannot be compared with the old pilot. Treat the new run as a fresh baseline and do not describe it as a before/after comparison.
incorrectAssumptions: That fixing the selector and regrading old snapshots will produce evidence about the guidance. It can only correct the grading of runs that never read the guidance. Keep that regrade reported separately from any claim about the treatment, and fix the regrading rules before looking at the results.

That 'Put the service call required to start a feature in its Application's prepareStart' is the framework's default. That is only true once an Application boundary is justified. Together with 'The Application calls a service/API module; Views receive data', it slightly overprescribes, and it conflicts with the earlier statement that 'a View with Regions is enough'. Condition it: 'When a feature has an Application, put …'.

That the MnObject row's 'synchronous destruction' is a meaningful selection criterion. The supplied contracts only say Application destruction is asynchronous. The rest is unverified and not useful for deciding when to pick MnObject.
missingTests: Link and anchor check across docs/ and llms.txt for every relative link and #fragment added in architecture.md.
Snapshot diff for each pilot condition, confirming the readme, quick-start and llms.txt links to architecture.md are present (or deliberately absent in control) exactly as the proposal defines.
Instrumentation dry run: one throwaway trajectory per condition, confirming doc-read events are captured before the frozen run.
Keep the installed-package probe as planned. It checks the runtime and examples, not what the prose teaches; say so in the proposal.
A leakage review of architecture.md against the rubric by someone not involved in writing either.
simplifications: Drop the Behavior and MnObject rows from the responsibility table. They aren't needed for ownership and lifetimes, and their claims are unverified. The API index already covers them.
Cut the 'Existing HTML can be a View's el …' paragraph. It is a view.md detail and does not belong in a concepts page.

Merge the overlapping-refresh paragraph into one sentence: 'For refreshes, decide which result may update state, how failure affects displayed data, and ensure completions after the owner ends have no effect.' Remove the closed-panel and initiating-View sentence.
Shorten the @mnjs/data paragraph to: 'Plain data suffices without observation; @mnjs/data provides observable Models/Collections but is not a full data layer—see provider contracts.'
In 'Let Views and Regions manage presentation', the empty-versus-selected detail sentence repeats the selection example in the previous section. Cut it.
nextSteps: Make the three accuracy edits (restart and children, conditional disposal, await stop() before an error View) and the prepareStart wording condition.
Check the unverified claims against view.md, behavior.md and mnobject.md, or remove them.
Run a link and anchor check, then the installed-package probe.
Get a leakage review from someone who hasn't seen the rubric, and rewrite the refresh guidance if needed.
Write the frozen run proposal with each condition's navigation snapshot, doc-read logging, and the old-snapshot regrade reported separately under grading rules fixed in advance.
